verses.zh: 亚兰王便・哈达聚集他的全军，率领三十二个王，带着车马上来围攻撒马利亚；
verses.en: Now King Ben Hadad of Syria assembled all his army, along with 32 other kings with their horses and chariots. He marched against Samaria[NOTE:1] and besieged and attacked it.[NOTE:2]
notes: For location see Map2-B1; Map4-D3; Map5-E2; Map6-A4; Map7-C1.
Heb “and he went up and besieged Samaria and fought against it.”

verses.zh: 又差遣使者进城见以色列王亚哈，对他说：「便・哈达如此说：
verses.en: He sent messengers to King Ahab of Israel, who was in the city.[NOTE:1] He said to him, “This is what Ben Hadad says:
notes: Heb “to the city.”

verses.zh: 你的金银都要归我，你妻子儿女中最美的也要归我。」
verses.en: ‘Your silver and your gold are mine, as well as the best of your wives and sons.’”

verses.zh: 以色列王回答说：「我主我王啊，可以依着你的话，我与我所有的都归你。」
verses.en: The king of Israel replied, “It is just as you say, my master, O king. I and all I own belong to you.”

verses.zh: 使者又来说：「便・哈达如此说：我已差遣人去见你，要你将你的金银、妻子、儿女都给我。
verses.en: The messengers came again and said, “This is what Ben Hadad says: ‘I sent this message to you, “You must give me your silver, gold, wives, and sons.”

verses.zh: 但明日约在这时候，我还要差遣臣仆到你那里，搜查你的家和你仆人的家，将你眼中一切所喜爱的都拿了去。」
verses.en: But now at this time tomorrow I will send my servants to you and they will search through your palace and your servants’ houses. They will carry away all your valuables.’”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “all that is desirable to your eyes they will put in their hand and take.”

verses.zh: 以色列王召了国中的长老来，对他们说：「请你们看看，这人是怎样地谋害我，他先差遣人到我这里来，要我的妻子、儿女，和金银，我并没有推辞他。」
verses.en: The king of Israel summoned all the leaders[NOTE:1] of the land and said, “Notice how this man is looking for trouble.[NOTE:2] Indeed, he demanded my wives, sons, silver, and gold, and I did not resist him.”
notes: Heb “elders.”
Heb “Know and see that this [man] is seeking trouble.”

verses.zh: 长老和百姓对王说：「不要听从他，也不要应允他。」
verses.en: All the leaders and people said to him, “Do not give in or agree to his demands.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Do not listen and do not be willing.”

verses.zh: 故此，以色列王对便・哈达的使者说：「你们告诉我主我王说：王头一次差遣人向仆人所要的，仆人都依从；但这次所要的，我不能依从。」使者就去回覆便・哈达。
verses.en: So he said to the messengers of Ben Hadad, “Say this to my master, the king: ‘I will give you everything you demanded at first from your servant, but I am unable to agree to this latest demand.’”[NOTE:1] So the messengers went back and gave their report.
notes: Heb “all which you sent to your servant in the beginning I will do, but this thing I am unable to do.”

verses.zh: 便・哈达又差遣人去见亚哈说：「撒马利亚的尘土若够跟从我的人每人捧一捧的，愿神明重重地降罚与我！」
verses.en: Ben Hadad sent another message to him, “May the gods judge me severely[NOTE:1] if there is enough dirt left in Samaria for all my soldiers to scoop up in their hands.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “So may the gods do to me, and so may they add.”
Heb “if the dirt of Samaria suffices for the handfuls of all the people who are at my feet.”

verses.zh: 以色列王说：「你告诉他说，才顶盔贯甲的，休要像摘盔卸甲的夸口。」
verses.en: The king of Israel replied, “Tell him the one who puts on his battle gear should not boast like one who is taking it off.”[NOTE:1]
notes: The point of the saying is that someone who is still preparing for a battle should not boast as if he has already won the battle. A modern parallel would be, “Don’t count your chickens before they’re hatched.”

verses.zh: 便・哈达和诸王正在帐幕里喝酒，听见这话，就对他臣仆说：「摆队吧！」他们就摆队攻城。
verses.en: When Ben Hadad received this reply,[NOTE:1] he and the other kings were drinking in their quarters.[NOTE:2] He ordered his servants, “Get ready to attack!” So they got ready to attack the city.
notes: Heb “When he heard this word.”
Heb “in the temporary shelters.” This is probably referring to tents.

verses.zh: 有一个先知来见以色列王亚哈，说：「耶和华如此说：『这一大群人你看见了吗？今日我必将他们交在你手里，你就知道我是耶和华。』」
verses.en: Now a prophet visited King Ahab of Israel and said, “This is what the Lord has said: ‘Do you see this huge army?[NOTE:1] Look, I am going to hand it over to you this very day. Then you will know that I am the Lord.’”
notes: Heb “see all this great horde.”

verses.zh: 亚哈说：「藉着谁呢？」他回答说：「耶和华说，藉着跟从省长的少年人。」亚哈说：「要谁率领呢？」他说：「要你亲自率领。」
verses.en: Ahab asked, “By whom will this be accomplished?”[NOTE:1] He answered, “This is what the Lord has said, ‘By the servants of the district governors.’” Ahab[NOTE:2] asked, “Who will launch the attack?” He answered, “You will.”
notes: The words “will this be accomplished” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
Heb “he”; the referent (Ahab) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 于是亚哈数点跟从省长的少年人，共有二百三十二名，后又数点以色列的众兵，共有七千名。
verses.en: So Ahab[NOTE:1] assembled the 232 servants of the district governors. After that he assembled all the Israelite army, numbering 7,000.
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Ahab) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 午间，他们就出城；便・哈达和帮助他的三十二个王正在帐幕里痛饮。
verses.en: They marched out at noon, while Ben Hadad and the 32 kings allied with him were drinking heavily[NOTE:1] in their quarters.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “drinking and drunken.”
Heb “in the temporary shelters.” This is probably referring to tents.

verses.zh: 跟从省长的少年人先出城；便・哈达差遣人去探望，他们回报说：「有人从撒马利亚出来了。」
verses.en: The servants of the district governors led the march. When Ben Hadad sent messengers, they reported back to him, “Men are marching out of Samaria.”[NOTE:1]
notes: For location see Map2-B1; Map4-D3; Map5-E2; Map6-A4; Map7-C1.

verses.zh: 他说：「他们若为讲和出来，要活捉他们；若为打仗出来，也要活捉他们。」
verses.en: He ordered, “Whether they come in peace or to do battle, take them alive.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “if they come in peace, take them alive; if they come for battle, take them alive.”

verses.zh: 跟从省长的少年人出城，军兵跟随他们；
verses.en: They marched out of the city with the servants of the district governors in the lead and the army behind them.

verses.zh: 各人遇见敌人就杀。亚兰人逃跑，以色列人追赶他们；亚兰王便・哈达骑着马和马兵一同逃跑。
verses.en: Each one struck down an enemy soldier;[NOTE:1] the Syrians fled and Israel chased them. King Ben Hadad of Syria escaped on horseback with some horsemen.
notes: Heb “each struck down his man.”

verses.zh: 以色列王出城攻打车马，大大击杀亚兰人。
verses.en: Then the king of Israel marched out and struck down the horses and chariots; he thoroughly defeated[NOTE:1] Syria.
notes: Heb “struck down Aram with a great striking down.”

verses.zh: 那先知来见以色列王，对他说：「你当自强，留心怎样防备；因为到明年这时候，亚兰王必上来攻击你。」
verses.en: The prophet[NOTE:1] visited the king of Israel and instructed him, “Go, fortify your defenses.[NOTE:2] Determine[NOTE:3] what you must do, for in the spring[NOTE:4] the king of Syria will attack[NOTE:5] you.”
notes: The definite article indicates previous reference, that is, “the prophet mentioned earlier” (see v. 13).
Heb “strengthen yourself.”
Heb “know and see.”
Heb “at the turning of the year.”
Heb “go up against.”

verses.zh: 亚兰王的臣仆对亚兰王说：「以色列人的神是山神，所以他们胜过我们；但在平原与他们打仗，我们必定得胜。
verses.en: Now the advisers[NOTE:1] of the king of Syria said to him: “Their God is a god of the mountains. That’s why they overpowered us. But if we fight them in the plains, we will certainly overpower them.
notes: Or “servants.”

verses.zh: 王当这样行：把诸王革去，派军长代替他们，
verses.en: So do this: Dismiss the kings from their command, and replace them with military commanders.

verses.zh: 又照着王丧失军兵之数，再招募一军，马补马，车补车，我们在平原与他们打仗，必定得胜。」王便听臣仆的话去行。
verses.en: Muster an army like the one you lost, with the same number of horses and chariots.[NOTE:1] Then we will fight them in the plains; we will certainly overpower them.” He approved their plan and did as they advised.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “And you, you muster an army like the one that fell from you, horse like horse and chariot like chariot.”
Heb “he listened to their voice and did so.”

verses.zh: 次年，便・哈达果然点齐亚兰人上亚弗去，要与以色列人打仗。
verses.en: In the spring[NOTE:1] Ben Hadad mustered the Syrian army[NOTE:2] and marched to Aphek to fight Israel.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “at the turning of the year.”
Heb “mustered Aram.”
Heb “and went up to Aphek for battle with Israel.”

verses.zh: 以色列人也点齐军兵，预备食物，迎着亚兰人出去，对着他们安营，好像两小群山羊羔；亚兰人却满了地面。
verses.en: When the Israelites had mustered and received their supplies, they marched out to face them in battle. When the Israelites deployed opposite them, they were like two small flocks[NOTE:1] of goats, but the Syrians filled the land.
notes: The noun translated “small flocks” occurs only here. The common interpretation derives the word from the verbal root חשׂף, “to strip off; to make bare.” In this case the noun refers to something “stripped off” or “made bare.” HALOT 359 s.v. II חשׂף derives the noun from a proposed homonymic verbal root (which occurs only in Ps 29:9) meaning “cause a premature birth.” In this case the derived noun could refer to goats that are undersized because they are born prematurely.

verses.zh: 有神人来见以色列王，说：「耶和华如此说：『亚兰人既说我―耶和华是山神，不是平原的神，所以我必将这一大群人都交在你手中，你们就知道我是耶和华。』」
verses.en: The prophet[NOTE:1] visited the king of Israel and said, “This is what the Lord has said: ‘Because the Syrians said, “The Lord is a god of the mountains and not a god of the valleys,” I will deliver this entire huge army into your control. Then you will know that I am the Lord.’”
notes: Heb “the man of God.”

verses.zh: 以色列人与亚兰人相对安营七日，到第七日两军交战；那一日以色列人杀了亚兰人步兵十万，
verses.en: The armies were deployed opposite each other for seven days. On the seventh day the battle began, and the Israelites killed 100,000 Syrian foot soldiers in one day.

verses.zh: 其余的逃入亚弗城；城墙塌倒，压死剩下的二万七千人。便・哈达也逃入城，藏在严密的屋子里。
verses.en: The remaining 27,000 ran to Aphek and went into the city, but the wall fell on them.[NOTE:1] Now Ben Hadad ran into the city and hid in an inner room.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and the remaining ones fled to Aphek to the city and the wall fell on 27,000 men, the ones who remained.”
Heb “and Ben Hadad fled and went into the city, [into] an inner room in an inner room.”

verses.zh: 他的臣仆对他说：「我们听说以色列王都是仁慈的王，现在我们不如腰束麻布，头套绳索，出去投降以色列王，或者他存留王的性命。」
verses.en: His advisers[NOTE:1] said to him, “Look, we have heard that the kings of the Israelite dynasty are kind.[NOTE:2] Allow us to put sackcloth around our waists and ropes on our heads[NOTE:3] and surrender[NOTE:4] to the king of Israel. Maybe he will spare our lives.”
notes: Or “servants.”

Heb “that the kings of the house of Israel, that kings of kindness [are] they.” Or “merciful” rather than “kind.” The word used here often means “devoted” or “loyal.” Perhaps the idea is that the Israelite kings are willing to make treaties with other kings.

Sackcloth was worn as a sign of sorrow and repentance. The precise significance of the ropes on the head is uncertain, but it probably was a sign of submission. These actions were comparable to raising a white flag on the battlefield or throwing in the towel in a boxing match.
Heb “go out.”

verses.zh: 于是他们腰束麻布，头套绳索，去见以色列王，说：「王的仆人便・哈达说，求王存留我的性命。」亚哈说：「他还活着吗？他是我的兄弟。」
verses.en: So they put sackcloth around their waists and ropes on their heads and went to the king of Israel. They said, “Your servant[NOTE:1] Ben Hadad says, ‘Please let me live!’” Ahab[NOTE:2] replied, “Is he still alive? He is my brother.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Your servant. By referring to Ben Hadad as Ahab’s servant, they are suggesting that Ahab make him a subject in a vassal treaty arrangement.
Heb “he”; the referent (Ahab) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
He is my brother. Ahab’s response indicates that he wants to make a parity treaty and treat Ben Hadad as an equal partner.

verses.zh: 这些人留心探出他的口气来，便急忙就着他的话说：「便・哈达是王的兄弟！」王说：「你们去请他来。」便・哈达出来见王，王就请他上车。
verses.en: The men took this as a good omen and quickly accepted his offer, saying, “Ben Hadad is your brother.” Ahab[NOTE:1] then said, “Go, get him.” So Ben Hadad came out to him, and Ahab pulled him up into his chariot.
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Ahab) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 便・哈达对王说：「我父从你父那里所夺的城邑，我必归还。你可以在大马士革立街市，像我父在撒马利亚所立的一样。」亚哈说：「我照此立约，放你回去」，就与他立约，放他去了。
verses.en: Ben Hadad[NOTE:1] said, “I will return the cities my father took from your father. You may set up markets[NOTE:2] in Damascus, just as my father did in Samaria.”[NOTE:3] Ahab then said, “I want to make a treaty with you before I dismiss you.”[NOTE:4] So he made a treaty with him and then dismissed him.
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Ben Hadad) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “streets,” but this must refer to streets set up with stalls for merchants to sell their goods. See HALOT 299 s.v. חוּץ.
For location see Map2-B1; Map4-D3; Map5-E2; Map6-A4; Map7-C1.

Heb “I will send you away with a treaty.” The words “Ahab then said” are supplied in the translation. There is nothing in the Hebrew text to indicate that the speaker has changed from Ben Hadad to Ahab. Some suggest adding “and he said” before “I will send you away.” Others prefer to maintain Ben Hadad as the speaker and change the statement to, “Please send me away with a treaty.”

verses.zh: 有先知的一个门徒奉耶和华的命对他的同伴说：「你打我吧！」那人不肯打他。
verses.en: One of the members of the prophetic guild[NOTE:1] told his companion a message from the Lord, “Please wound me!” But the man refused to wound him.
notes: Heb “of the sons of the prophets.”

verses.zh: 他就对那人说：「你既不听从耶和华的话，你一离开我，必有狮子咬死你。」那人一离开他，果然遇见狮子，把他咬死了。
verses.en: So the prophet[NOTE:1] said to him, “Because you have disobeyed the Lord, as soon as you leave me a lion will kill you.” When he left him, a lion attacked and killed him.
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (the prophet) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 先知的门徒又遇见一个人，对他说：「你打我吧！」那人就打他，将他打伤。
verses.en: He found another man and said, “Wound me!” So the man wounded him severely.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and the man wounded him, wounding and bruising.”

verses.zh: 他就去了，用头巾蒙眼，改换面目，在路旁等候王。
verses.en: The prophet then went and stood by the road, waiting for the king. He also disguised himself by putting a bandage down over his eyes.

verses.zh: 王从那里经过，他向王呼叫说：「仆人在阵上的时候，有人带了一个人来，对我说：『你看守这人，若把他失了，你的性命必代替他的性命；不然，你必交出一他连得银子来。』
verses.en: When the king passed by, he called out to the king, “Your servant went out into the heat[NOTE:1] of the battle, and then a man turned aside and brought me a prisoner.[NOTE:2] He told me, ‘Guard this prisoner. If he ends up missing for any reason,[NOTE:3] you will pay with your life or with a talent[NOTE:4] of silver.’[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “middle.”
Heb “man” (also a second time later in this verse).
Heb “if being missed, he is missed.” The emphatic infinitive absolute before the finite verbal form lends solemnity to the warning.

The Hebrew term כִּכָּר (kikkar, “circle”) refers generally to something that is round. When used of metals it can refer to a disk-shaped weight made of the metal or to a standard unit of weight, generally regarded as a talent. Since the accepted weight for a talent of metal is about 75 pounds, this would have amounted to about 75 pounds of silver.
Heb “your life will be in place of his life, or a unit of silver you will pay.”

verses.zh: 仆人正在忙乱之间，那人就不见了。」以色列王对他说：「你自己定妥了，必照样判断你。」
verses.en: Well, it just so happened that while your servant was doing this and that, he disappeared.” The king of Israel said to him, “Your punishment is already determined by your own testimony.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “so [i.e., in accordance with his testimony] is your judgment, you have determined [it].”

verses.zh: 他急忙除掉蒙眼的头巾，以色列王就认出他是一个先知。
verses.en: The prophet[NOTE:1] quickly removed the bandage from his eyes, and the king of Israel recognized he was one of the prophets.
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (the prophet) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 他对王说：「耶和华如此说：『因你将我定要灭绝的人放去，你的命就必代替他的命，你的民也必代替他的民。』」
verses.en: The prophet[NOTE:1] then said to him, “This is what the Lord has said: ‘Because you released a man I had determined should die, you will pay with your life, and your people will suffer instead of his people.’”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (the prophet) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

Heb “Because you sent away the man of my destruction [i.e., that I determined should be destroyed] from [my/your?] hand, your life will be in place of his life, and your people in place of his people.”

verses.zh: 于是以色列王闷闷不乐地回到撒马利亚，进了他的宫。
verses.en: The king of Israel went home to Samaria[NOTE:1] bitter and angry.
notes: For location see Map2-B1; Map4-D3; Map5-E2; Map6-A4; Map7-C1.
